div.head: Northu 56
div.ab: Se þe ænig þissa do, gilde wite: friman XII ór, ðeowman ða hyde; — buton wegferende, þa moton for neode meteneade ferian; ⁊ for unfriðe man mot freolsæfenan nide fulfaran betweonan Eferwic ⁊ six mila gemete.

Se þe ænig þissa do, gilde wite: friman XII or, ðeowman ða hyde; buton wegferende, þa moton for neode mete ferian; and for unfriðe man mot freolsæfenan nide fulfaran betweonan Eferwic and six mila gemete.

Wer etwas hiervon thut, zahle Strafe: ein Freier 12 Ör, ein Sklav die Haut [Prügel]; — ausgenommen Reisende, die aus Nothwendigkeit Lebensmittel-Bedarf(?) führen dürfen; und Krieges wegen darf man an Feiertags-Vorabenden im Nothfall reisen zwischen York und 6 Meilen Entfernung.

Whoever does any of these things, let him pay a fine: a freeman 12 ores, a slave his hide [a flogging]; — except travellers, who may out of necessity carry needful provisions(?); and on account of war one may, in case of need, travel on the eves of feast-days between York and a distance of six miles.

He who does any of these things is to pay the penalty: a freeman 12 ores, a slave with a flogging; except for travellers, who are permitted to carry sustenance for their needs; and in case of hostility one may travel because of necessity between York and a distance of six miles on the eve of festivals.

One who does any of these is to pay a penalty: a freeman twelve oras, a slave with a beating; except for travelers, who may carry food out of necessity. And in times of conflict one may, out of necessity, journey a distance of up to six miles from York on the eve of a holy day.
div.note: Liebermann thinks ‘neade’ in ‘meteneade’ is perhaps a dittography of the preceding ‘neode’ and should be struck. Liebermann compares EGu 7.1.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘He who does any of these things is to pay the penalty: a freemen 12 ores, a slave with a flogging; except for travellers, who are permitted to carry sustenance for their needs; and in case of hostility one may travel because of necessity between York and a distance of six miles on the eve of festivals.’).; AY: corrected against Rabin p. 312 / 313, October 2026 (was “The Obligations of Individuals and On Reeves”, now “∅”)

note.seg: neade vielleicht als Dittographie des vorherigen neode zu streichen.
neade perhaps to be deleted as a dittography of the preceding neode.
Die durch II Cn 45, 1ff. zu EGu gemachten Zusätze fehlen hier; jener ist also wohl nicht benutzt
The additions made to EGu by II Cn 45, 1ff. are absent here; the latter has therefore probably not been used
Aus EGu 7; nur wird der Ausdruck Rechtsbruchbusse durch deren Betrag ersetzt; auch u. 57
From EGu 7; only the term ‘compensation for breach of law’ is replaced by its amount; also below 57

for neode . . neade scheint mir bedenklich; Schmid übs es ‘wegen Mangels, notwendig’; ‘compelled by circumstances to supply their needs’ Toller 718; dagegen nur eines ‘in case of need’ übs. Thorpe. Neod kann ‘Lebensnotdurft’ bedeuten, laut der Zitate bei Toller nur mit Genetiv des Bedürftigen daneben, doch to neode Ke 956. Nied kann in Einem Satz zweierlei bedeuten: nolde Maurus faran for nanre neode butan he nyde scolde; Ælfric Saints ed. Skeat 164

for neode . . neade seems questionable to me; Schmid translates it ‘wegen Mangels, notwendig’; ‘compelled by circumstances to supply their needs’ Toller 718; Thorpe, on the other hand, translates only one of them, ‘in case of need’. Neod can mean ‘necessaries of life’, according to the quotations in Toller only with a genitive of the person in need beside it, yet to neode Ke 956. Nied can mean two different things in one and the same sentence: nolde Maurus faran for nanre neode butan he nyde scolde; Ælfric Saints ed. Skeat 164
Das Compositum fehlt zwar Toller, Sweet, aber s. Wb full- und bei Toller full(ge)gan(gan) ‘nachgehen, verfolgen, ausführen, vollenden’, fullfleon ‘ganz fliehen’
The compound is indeed missing from Toller and Sweet, but see Wb full-, and in Toller full(ge)gan(gan) ‘follow, pursue, carry out, complete’, fullfleon ‘flee completely’
